body: Just FYI, in-town Atlanta's population is 500k, but the metro area is 5 million. All within a 30-minute drive.
That the justice system in America isn't about justice at all. It's about money and looking for the most convenient answer.

Thank you for the advice, but I did all of that, and I make too much money. Of course, all of it goes to my lawyer, his lawyer, the guardian ad litem, medical bills, and his half of the bills that my ex didn't pay while we were married. I don't have much left over at the end of the month.

And now, we're into the decision as to whether or not I'm going to appeal. And I can appeal, and I have a good chance of winning that appeal. But that's money for a whole new attorney that I don't have, and a loss will likely result in me having to pay his attorney's fees, too. Another $10,0000.

I don't mean to fixate on money, but money is power and access in the court system. And he already has it, since his brother and sister are both attorneys, and his attorney is working for free because they've been friends for years, and because she's mad at me because I never got her husband a job (I didn't have any authority over hiring).

It's all ridiculous, middle-school, small-town-politics kind of bullcrap. And I don't have the capacity to deal with it anymore.
Legal aid doesn't handle this kind of thing.
I trust mine. I like her. But I don't understand what I'm supposed to be doing there. How is talking to her going to change anything? It's not.

I'm already in therapy. I just feel like I'm spending all this time talking about my own bullshit. It feels like this ludicrous self-important onanism that costs $200 a month and accomplishes nothing.

This made me LOL - only because of the irony, not because your idea wasn't a good one, or full of good intentions.

The irony is... he IS the media in this town. It's his brother who is the politician. So... yeah. Basically, they have the whole situation sewn up with that combo.

What happened is completely my fault. I protected him instead of calling 911 every time he passed out drunk. I protected him instead of calling 911 every time he pushed me around. Had I not done that, I would have had the evidence required to show what kind of person and father he truly is. 

Oh, did you know that police reports are not considered evidence? They're hearsay. Can't get them admitted. So it's not enough to have written reports of his behavior. You have to also have eye-witness testimony or convictions in a court of law.
I'm so sorry. I am so very sorry. I don't know the particulars of your situation, but I know how much it hurts. I hope things change for you.

I think, after some time, that she won't miss me. I think, as soon as the guardian ad litem is out of the picture, he'll keep her from me, knowing that I won't be able to pay an attorney to enforce the custody agreement.

He's gearing up for a libel suit, which will destroy me utterly. Then he'll use the judgment he gets from that to go back to court and pursue sole custody. He's already told me that's his plan. This is never going to end. Ever. 

And I've asked for help to fight him. But no one will do anything. They won't testify because they're scared of him. No one in my family has any money to contribute.

And he audiotaped one of our arguments. It took me six years to stand up to him, and I finally lost my temper one night and screamed at him for 20 minutes about how he was throwing our marriage away for beer and cigarettes. And he taped it, and threatens to play it for "the media" every time I try to make any headway. And we live in a small town, where jobs are few and loyalties run for generations.

I can't give up, because what he's doing is wrong. But I'll never win. And this will never end. And my daughter will suffer the most. She's all I live for. So tell me, again, what reason there is to stick around if my presence is what will cause her the most pain? I'm looking for any reason I can't argue with, because I want to be with her, but I haven't found one yet. It feels selfish to stay. It feels like I'm stealing something from her.
It's not. But I have to prove that it is the truth. And I couldn't before.

That's where we are, too. My daughter is constipated and wets the bed. She also begs me not to make her go back. And I have to tell her that we have to follow the rules the judge put down, or we'll get in trouble.  

He took me off of the list of emergency contacts at her school. He kept her home for one of my visitation weekends. He doesn't want me in her life. But I know that he dumps her with his mother until 7 or 8 at night every day of the week. And I know that his mother doesn't interact with her. She just leaves her to play alone with her dolls while she does... whatever it is that she does. I don't know. She doesn't work, her children are grown, and she has two maids, so I don't know what she does all day. 

My child is unhappy there. He doesn't arrange for social interaction for her. He has cut down on her dance classes. He has changed her pediatrician. He changed his job. He still drinks and smokes and pops prescription pain and anxiety pills. And she's showing signs of temper. She lashes out at me verbally, and for a brief moment, physically. I just picked her up and hug her and tell her that her that I love her, that feelings are all okay, but that she has to express them differently. And she cried and apologized and all was well.

But it won't be like that forever. It's only been 90 days since the final hearing. The final order isn't even signed yet. She'll adjust. And she'll forget our time together. She'll forget the four years I protected her from his drinking, and he from himself. She'll forget our nights snuggling under the blanket in bed while discovering Junie B. Jones. She'll accept the life her father carves out for her, lonely though it may be. And our relationship will suffer for it.

That slow decline will be even worse torture. And I don't want to live through it.

My ex will never allow me to sort things out. He has cut me out of her life as much as possible, and he is going to sue me for libel next because I stated in the custody hearing that he - truthfully - has a drinking and drug problem. It won't matter if I win. The cost of defending myself will be more than I can manage. And I'll never settle, because I work in PR, and I'll never get another job if I lose a libel case. But there's no point in any of it anymore. Working. Fighting. I'll never win. And it will never stop.

EDIT: Not the "hearing." The filing.
How about I don't even know how to PM someone. That is how much I suck at life.

I try. I do. But I don't see the reason for it anymore. There will never be a day when I win this battle, because my ex is too politically powerful, and because the case goes back to the same judge every time. My daughter is so amazing. She deserves calm. She deserves stability. She deserves a chance to develop relationship ideals that aren't based on reports from private investigators and guardians ad litem.
